lesson_title: Four Engines: SA's Industrial Regions, SDIs and IDZs
hook_text: No port. No river. A third of the economy lives up there anyway. How?
clip_script: Gauteng is the strangest industrial giant anywhere. It has no port — a factory in Kempton Park sends its exports six hundred kilometres downhill to Durban before they smell the sea. It has no great river — its water is pumped up from the Vaal Dam and even from the mountains of Lesotho, like a house drinking through a very long straw. By every textbook rule, nothing this size should stand on that plateau. So why does a third of the economy sit up there? Because of what the gold left behind: the railways still meet there, the skills still live there, the richest market in Africa still shops there. The engine outlived the gold that built it.
visual_style: Night satellite zoom to the blazing highveld, water animating uphill from Lesotho's peaks, rail lines converging on Johannesburg like spokes to a hub.
mood: Awe with a puzzle at its heart.
pacing: Pose the impossibility, stack the missing pieces, resolve with the gold's legacy.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — four core regions, two case studies, and the SDI and IDZ plans to spread the map.
